concepts.def: Holiday vocabulary: pasé una semana en la costa (I spent a week on the coast), tomar el sol (to sunbathe), hacer turismo (to sightsee).
Places to stay: el hotel, el camping, una pensión (guesthouse), el albergue juvenil (youth hostel), reservar una habitación.
Describe past holiday weather with the imperfect: hacía sol, hacía buen tiempo; single events use the preterite: ayer llovió.
Describe your area: 'Vivo en el norte de Irlanda', 'Mi ciudad está situada en la costa', las afueras, el paisaje (landscape).
In holiday accounts, the preterite reports completed events (visité, fui) while the imperfect sets the scene (era, había, hacía).
Tourist office phrases: un plano de la ciudad (a city map), un folleto (a leaflet), '¿A qué hora abre el museo?'

walkthroughs.body_html:
Topic 1: Home and Abroad — a core area of GCSE Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Topic 1: Home and Abroad brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Topic 1: Home and Abroad.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: 'Tomé el sol en la playa' means what?
options: I sunbathed on the beach
I drank juice on the beach
I took photos of the beach
I got sunburnt at home

mcqs.q: Why is the imperfect used in 'Hacía sol todos los días'?
options: It describes ongoing or repeated weather in the past
It refers to the future
It is a command
It shows a single completed action

mcqs.q: 'El albergue juvenil' is what kind of accommodation?
options: A youth hostel
A luxury hotel
A campsite
A holiday apartment

mcqs.q: 'Mi ciudad está situada en el norte' means what?
options: My town is located in the north
My town is sitting on a mountain
My town used to be in the north
My town will move north

mcqs.q: Which past tense sets the scene in a holiday account?
options: The preterite is used for everything that happened in the past.
A plant for your hotel room.
Spanish has only one past tense, like English.
The imperfect describes background and ongoing situations (hacía sol, había mucha gente), while the preterite reports completed events (visité, fui).

mcqs.q: What is 'un plano' at the tourist office?
options: A street map of the city.
A plant for your hotel room.
Spanish has only one past tense, like English.
A plane, because of the similar spelling.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between 'la playa' and 'la plaza'?
options: They are two spellings of the same word for beach.
La plaza means the swimming pool.
A plant for your hotel room.
La playa is the beach; la plaza is the town square.
